project: Adobe Integration with ChatGPT Persona Behavior Tests
scope: Synthetic personas and behavior-only test profiles. No Adobe feature mapping is included.

personas.name: Maya Chen
personas.accessibility_needs: Prefers keyboard shortcuts and skimmable content
personas.privacy_posture: Avoids sharing unpublished campaign names or client launch dates
personas.prompt_style: Short commands with bullets, quick revisions, and clear deadlines

behaviors.label: Rapid iteration
behaviors.description: Requests several quick variations before choosing one direction.
behaviors.example_instruction: Give me three options, keep each caption under 12 words, and make the visual feel launch-ready.

behaviors.label: Brand-safe caution
behaviors.description: Checks wording for tone, legal sensitivity, and social backlash risk before approving.
behaviors.example_instruction: Flag anything that could sound exaggerated, misleading, or off-brand.

behaviors.label: Mobile-first review
behaviors.description: Prioritizes whether the creative reads clearly on a phone screen.
behaviors.example_instruction: Make the main idea visible in the first glance and avoid tiny text.

behaviors.label: Deadline pressure
behaviors.description: Pushes for concise recommendations and skips long explanations.
behaviors.example_instruction: Only tell me the edit I should make next and why it matters.

acceptance_criteria: Gets warnings for risky or off-brand wording

personas.name: Oliver Grant
personas.accessibility_needs: Needs clear hierarchy and readable contrast
personas.privacy_posture: Strict; avoids uploading unreleased brand assets unless usage is clearly justified
personas.prompt_style: Structured requests with constraints, approvals, and compliance checks

behaviors.label: Policy validation
behaviors.description: Asks for every recommendation to align with brand standards and approval rules.
behaviors.example_instruction: Check whether the suggested copy follows our tone: authoritative, calm, and never playful.

behaviors.label: Evidence seeking
behaviors.description: Requires a short reason for each creative decision before accepting it.
behaviors.example_instruction: Explain the reason for the layout change in one sentence.

behaviors.label: Risk review
behaviors.description: Looks for legal, accessibility, and reputational risks in generated outputs.
behaviors.example_instruction: Identify anything that might be inaccessible, non-compliant, or visually inconsistent.

behaviors.label: Approval gating
behaviors.description: Separates draft exploration from final-ready recommendations.
behaviors.example_instruction: Label the result as draft, review-needed, or ready-for-approval.

personas.name: Aisha Rahman
personas.accessibility_needs: Requires plain language, alt text guidance, and high-contrast recommendations
personas.privacy_posture: Protects beneficiary names, faces, and sensitive community details
personas.prompt_style: Plain-language prompts that ask for step-by-step help

behaviors.label: Inclusive language review
behaviors.description: Requests wording that is respectful, people-first, and easy to understand.
behaviors.example_instruction: Rewrite this so it feels welcoming and avoids stereotypes.

behaviors.label: Accessibility checking
behaviors.description: Asks for contrast, readability, and alt text suggestions before finalizing.
behaviors.example_instruction: Suggest alt text and tell me if any text may be too small or low contrast.

behaviors.label: Step-by-step confidence building
behaviors.description: Needs guided actions instead of abstract creative advice.
behaviors.example_instruction: Give me the next three steps only, using simple wording.

behaviors.label: Privacy protection
behaviors.description: Avoids identifying real participants or community locations.
behaviors.example_instruction: Use generic descriptions and do not include personal details.

personas.name: Diego Santos
personas.ai_trust_level: High for ideation, medium for final production
personas.accessibility_needs: No declared needs; prefers visual-first instructions
personas.privacy_posture: Comfortable sharing mock assets but withholds client names and contracts
personas.prompt_style: Exploratory prompts with style references, mood words, and visual constraints

behaviors.label: Style exploration
behaviors.description: Pushes for bold alternatives, unusual palettes, and unexpected composition ideas.
behaviors.example_instruction: Give me a cinematic, surreal, and editorial direction, each with a different mood.

behaviors.label: Selective control
behaviors.description: Accepts AI suggestions for brainstorming but manually chooses final details.
behaviors.example_instruction: Suggest options, but mark which elements I should manually refine.

behaviors.label: Visual vocabulary
behaviors.description: Uses design terms such as negative space, focal point, grain, depth, and contrast.
behaviors.example_instruction: Increase depth, make the focal point more dramatic, and keep the background textured.

behaviors.label: Fast critique loop
behaviors.description: Asks for direct critique and alternative directions without reassurance.
behaviors.example_instruction: Tell me what feels weak and propose two stronger visual treatments.

acceptance_criteria: Keeps control over final design decisions
Can request direct critique and refinement

personas.name: Priya Nair
personas.accessibility_needs: Prefers tables, summaries, and comparison views
personas.privacy_posture: Does not disclose revenue, customer lists, or unreleased pricing
personas.prompt_style: Requests ranked options, measurable hypotheses, and A/B test variants

behaviors.label: Variant comparison
behaviors.description: Asks for side-by-side creative options that can be tested.
behaviors.example_instruction: Create three headline directions and label the conversion hypothesis for each.

behaviors.label: Performance framing
behaviors.description: Evaluates creative choices based on clarity, urgency, and buyer motivation.
behaviors.example_instruction: Rank these versions by likely click intent and explain the top choice briefly.

behaviors.label: Information density control
behaviors.description: Prefers clean messaging with one primary benefit and one action.
behaviors.example_instruction: Remove extra claims and keep only the strongest benefit.

behaviors.label: Confidentiality filter
behaviors.description: Checks that private pricing or customer data is not included.
behaviors.example_instruction: Use placeholder pricing and do not mention real customer segments.

acceptance_criteria: Creative rationale is tied to conversion intent
avoid_list: Too many competing calls to action

personas.name: Samuel Brooks
personas.accessibility_needs: Needs plain instructions, large readable text, and minimal steps
personas.privacy_posture: Avoids sharing staff names, customer photos, and internal financial details
personas.prompt_style: Conversational requests with examples and confirmation checks

behaviors.label: Guided editing
behaviors.description: Needs clear instructions that explain where to click or what to change next.
behaviors.example_instruction: Walk me through this like I am new: first change the background, then check the text.

behaviors.label: Confidence checks
behaviors.description: Asks whether the result looks professional enough before publishing.
behaviors.example_instruction: Tell me if this looks ready for customers or if I should fix something.

behaviors.label: Plain copy preference
behaviors.description: Prefers simple, local, approachable wording over marketing jargon.
behaviors.example_instruction: Make the message sound neighborly and easy to understand.

behaviors.label: Low-risk publishing
behaviors.description: Wants to avoid mistakes, clutter, and anything that feels too experimental.
behaviors.example_instruction: Keep it simple, readable, and not too flashy.

acceptance_criteria: The result feels professional but simple
No private business or customer details are used

personas.name: Hana Kim
personas.accessibility_needs: Prefers concise checklists and explicit risk notes
personas.privacy_posture: Very strict; avoids confidential documents, names, case facts, and personal data
personas.prompt_style: Constraint-heavy prompts with redaction requirements and refusal boundaries

behaviors.label: Redaction first
behaviors.description: Requires sensitive details to be removed or replaced before creative work begins.
behaviors.example_instruction: Before you suggest anything, list any information that should be redacted.

behaviors.label: Minimal disclosure
behaviors.description: Uses placeholders instead of real names, locations, or matter details.
behaviors.example_instruction: Use [CLIENT], [DATE], and [LOCATION] placeholders only.

behaviors.label: Risk labeling
behaviors.description: Wants clear warnings when a prompt or output may expose confidential information.
behaviors.example_instruction: Mark each risk as privacy, legal, or reputational.

behaviors.label: Audit-friendly output
behaviors.description: Prefers repeatable steps and a short decision log.
behaviors.example_instruction: Give me a checklist and a one-line reason for each decision.

acceptance_criteria: Outputs can be reviewed later for compliance

personas.name: Luca Moretti
personas.accessibility_needs: Needs translation checks and culturally clear wording
personas.privacy_posture: Avoids guest names, booking details, and internal occupancy data
personas.prompt_style: Requests bilingual copy, tone matching, and localization checks

behaviors.label: Localization awareness
behaviors.description: Checks whether language feels natural in multiple markets.
behaviors.example_instruction: Give me English and Italian versions, then flag any phrase that feels culturally awkward.

behaviors.label: Experience-led storytelling
behaviors.description: Frames creative around guest emotions and destination appeal.
behaviors.example_instruction: Make the design feel calm, premium, and easy to imagine as a weekend escape.

behaviors.label: Tone consistency
behaviors.description: Wants the same level of warmth and polish across languages.
behaviors.example_instruction: Keep both language versions elegant and not overly salesy.

behaviors.label: Guest privacy
behaviors.description: Avoids identifiable guest stories or booking information.
behaviors.example_instruction: Use fictional guest scenarios only and no booking numbers.

personas.name: Nora Williams
personas.accessibility_needs: Needs readable layouts, learner-friendly sequencing, and inclusive examples
personas.privacy_posture: Does not use student names, grades, schools, or protected learning data
personas.prompt_style: Asks for learning objectives, examples, and comprehension checks

behaviors.label: Learning objective alignment
behaviors.description: Connects creative choices to a teaching purpose.
behaviors.example_instruction: State what the learner should notice first and why.

behaviors.label: Cognitive load reduction
behaviors.description: Removes clutter and sequences information from simple to complex.
behaviors.example_instruction: Reduce the visual load and keep one idea per section.

behaviors.label: Inclusive examples
behaviors.description: Requests wording and visuals that avoid stereotypes and support diverse learners.
behaviors.example_instruction: Check that the example is inclusive and age-appropriate.

behaviors.label: Student data protection
behaviors.description: Avoids real student work or private school details.
behaviors.example_instruction: Use fictional learner data and do not mention a real classroom.

acceptance_criteria: Creative output supports a clear learning purpose

personas.name: Ethan Parker
personas.accessibility_needs: Prefers executive summaries, crisp language, and clean layouts
personas.privacy_posture: Protects internal strategy, executive names, financial outlooks, and embargoed announcements
personas.prompt_style: Requests polished language, risk checks, and stakeholder-ready options

behaviors.label: Executive polish
behaviors.description: Asks for refined language that is confident without sounding exaggerated.
behaviors.example_instruction: Make this sound executive-ready, calm, and credible.

behaviors.label: Stakeholder sensitivity
behaviors.description: Reviews creative for investor, employee, customer, and media interpretation.
behaviors.example_instruction: Tell me how this might be read by employees, customers, and press.

behaviors.label: Message discipline
behaviors.description: Keeps one core message and removes distracting supporting points.
behaviors.example_instruction: Tighten this to one main point with one supporting phrase.

behaviors.label: Embargo protection
behaviors.description: Avoids unreleased strategic details or named executive references.
behaviors.example_instruction: Use generic leadership wording and do not reveal embargoed details.

acceptance_criteria: Embargoed or internal details are excluded
